title: What Is a Mechanic Salary? Award Rates, Casual Loading, and Annual Pay
description: Learn how to calculate a mechanic salary from hourly rates under the Vehicle Repair Award. Compare award rates, casual loading, and the National Minimum Wage for 2026.
salarySummary: A mechanic salary under the Vehicle Repair, Services and Retail Award ranges from $29.45 to $32.22 per hour for tradespersons, based on 38 ordinary hours per week.

faqs.q: What is the casual loading for mechanics under the award?
faqs.a: Under the Vehicle Repair, Services and Retail Award 2020, casual mechanics receive a 25% loading on the base hourly rate for ordinary hours worked Monday to Friday between 6.00 am and 6.00 pm. Higher loadings apply for evening, Saturday, Sunday, and public holiday work. The loading is paid instead of annual leave, personal leave, and other entitlements.

faqs.q: How does the National Minimum Wage compare to the mechanic award rate?
faqs.a: From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour (or $1004.90 per week for 38 hours). The Vehicle Repair Award sets higher minimum rates for mechanics: a Level I tradesperson (R6) earns $29.45 per hour, and a Level II tradesperson (R7) earns $32.22 per hour. Award rates always override the national minimum for covered employees.

faqs.q: Is superannuation included in the hourly rate?
faqs.a: No, superannuation is paid on top of the hourly rate. Under the Superannuation Guarantee, employers must contribute 12% of ordinary earnings (up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year) to a complying super fund. This is separate from the base wage or salary.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding a Mechanic Salary

If you're trying to work out a **mechanic salary** from an hourly rate, the key is knowing which pay structure applies. Most mechanics in Australia are covered by the **Vehicle Repair, Services and Retail Award 2020**, which sets minimum hourly rates for different skill levels. For employees not covered by any award, the **National Minimum Wage** applies. This guide explains how to convert an hourly rate to annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures, and what to expect for tax and super.

### Hourly to Annual: The Basic Formula

The standard calculation is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

We assume a full-time employee works **38 ordinary hours per week** (the standard under the Vehicle Repair Award and the National Minimum Wage). For example, a Level I tradesperson mechanic on $29.45 per hour would earn:

- Weekly: $29.45 × 38 = $1,119.10
- Fortnightly: $1,119.10 × 2 = $2,238.20
- Annual: $1,119.10 × 52 = $58,193.20

This formula assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. Use [the timesheet](/) to quickly test different hourly rates.

### Award Rates vs. National Minimum Wage

The **National Minimum Wage** from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour (or $1004.90 per week for 38 hours). However, the Vehicle Repair Award sets higher minimums for mechanics. The award classifies employees into wage groups R1 to R7. A qualified mechanic is typically a **tradesperson Level I (R6)** at $29.45 per hour or **Level II (R7)** at $32.22 per hour. These rates are the minimum; many employers pay above award.

If you're a casual mechanic, the award adds a **25% loading** on the base rate for ordinary hours worked Monday to Friday between 6 am and 6 pm. For example, a casual R6 mechanic would receive $29.45 × 1.25 = $36.81 per hour during those times. Higher loadings apply for other shifts. The National Minimum Wage also has a 25% casual loading, bringing it to $33.05 per hour.

### What About Fortnightly Pay?

Many employers pay wages fortnightly. Under the award, wages can be paid weekly, fortnightly, or monthly by agreement. To get a fortnightly figure, simply double the weekly amount. For a full-time R7 mechanic on $32.22 per hour:

- Weekly: $32.22 × 38 = $1,224.36
- Fortnightly: $1,224.36 × 2 = $2,448.72

Check our [pay guides](/blog) for more on award-specific pay periods.

### Tax and Super

Once you have your annual gross figure, you can estimate **take-home pay** using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- Nil tax on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus a **Medicare levy** of 2% (based on 2025–26 single reduction thresholds).

**Superannuation** is paid on top of your base wage. The **Superannuation Guarantee** rate is 12% of ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For a mechanic earning $58,193 annually, the employer would contribute an extra $6,983.16 to super. This is not deducted from your pay; it's an additional benefit. See our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page for more.

### Casual Loading and Super

Casual loading (25% under the award) is included in your ordinary earnings for super purposes. So a casual mechanic on $36.81 per hour would have super calculated on that rate. The loading itself does not attract extra super; it's simply part of the hourly wage.

### Using the Calculator

Our [the timesheet](/) lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add the 25% casual loading. It then shows weekly, fortnightly, and annual figures, along with estimated tax and super. Remember: the results are estimates. They assume you work 38 hours every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted.

### Reference Tables

For a full list of award classifications and rates, see our [reference tables](/data). The Fair Work Commission also publishes a **Modern Awards Pay Database** with calculated minimum rates, allowances, and penalties. Always check the award itself for your exact classification.

### Summary

A **mechanic salary** under the Vehicle Repair Award starts at $29.45 per hour for a Level I tradesperson. Using the 38-hour week, that's about $58,200 per year before tax and super. Casual mechanics get an extra 25% loading. The National Minimum Wage is lower at $26.44 per hour, but award-covered employees must receive at least the award rate. Use the formula hourly × 38 × 52 to get your annual figure, and remember super is paid on top.
